builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: How Do Deep Networks Encode and Selectively Use Information? Shared Encoding and Conditional Signed Readout in Vision and Language Models
summary: The method replaces heuristic or magnitude-based channel-importance scoring with a criterion combining conditional channel variance and fixed downstream readout weights, and replaces generic activation patching with signed channel/pathway decomposition for interpreting edits. It costs substantial per-model analysis effort: perturbation experiments, disjoint block probing, and unit-group selection, with no turnkey implementation or validated pipeline for arbitrary production models. It can fail because the findings are demonstrated on specific convolutional classifiers, one vision transformer, and Qwen2.5 with particular prompt setups; antagonistic-unit structure and prompt-presentation reversals may not transfer, and misidentified signed groups could degrade rather than preserve pruned-model behavior.
rationale: The paper is a mechanistic analysis of shared encoding and signed readout, and its only production-adjacent result—predicting single-channel pruning recovery from conditional variance and readout weights—is validated on ten cuts in a research setting rather than as a deployable pruning method.
technique: Signed channel readout analysis for pruning prediction
